classification.difficultyReason: Use the explicit Pythagoras hint to obtain the equilateral-triangle altitude, then calculate area and prism volume.

inlines.text: Determine the volume of this equilateral triangular prism. Answer to 1 d.p.
(hint: you need to use Pythagoras’ theorem)

spec.description: Equilateral triangular prism extending upper-right, three matching double ticks on the near triangle and three dashed concealed edges meeting at the hidden rear vertex.
spec.mathematics: Explicit equilateral 4 m cross-section with altitude sqrt(12) and 10 m depth; undistorted front view and uniformly receding depth. Numerical triangle and 3D visibility gates remain required.
spec.answerVisibility: Only 4 m, 10 m and equal-side marks appear. No solution altitude or half-base is added to the question diagram.

answer.worked:
The perpendicular altitude bisects the equilateral triangle’s $4\text{ m}$ base.
$$\begin{align*}h^2+2^2&=4^2\\h^2&=12\\h&=\sqrt{12}\text{ m}\\A&=\frac{4\sqrt{12}}{2}\\A&=4\sqrt3\text{ m}^2\\V&=Ah\\V&=4\sqrt3\times10\\V&=40\sqrt3\text{ m}^3\\V&\approx69.3\text{ m}^3\quad\text{(1 d.p.)}\end{align*}$$
